thread:
lia: Heads-up: I'm proposing we add a compact cost-hint header at the edge so downstream joins don't need expensive late lookups. This is a follow-up to the RFC — focusing on signer rotation, HMAC validity window, and TLV extensibility. Short ask: review the tradeoffs and suggest missing failure modes.

pranav: quick note: i'm +1 on reducing late joins. question: why not push resolution to a sidecar next to application instead of the global proxy? Sidecar keeps per-service policies and avoids cross-proxy signer issues.

lia: good point. tradeoffs: sidecar gives locality but slower rollout (needs per-service changes) and more infra to manage. global proxy gives one place to reason about resolve cache, consistent signer, and consistent header format. We think global proxy is better for initial rollout.

matt: Perf hit estimate? we need median and tail. Also curious about worst-case if cache misses spike.

sara: proto bench: on a small node prototype: cache hit median +120us, p95 +400us. Cache miss path (remote lookup) adds ~8-12ms. We'll add circuit-breaker to avoid blocking ingest: attach header only when fast-path returns, else continue without header and emit fallback metric.

lia: header format proposal (TLV-ish simple KV):
```
X-RW-COST: v=1;tk=tb_9x3;rv=20260301;sig=base64(hmac);f=ph
```
fields: v=version, tk=billing token, rv=resolve version (dateish), sig=signature, f=flags (ph=pii-hashed). Parsers must ignore unknown fields.

pranav: signature rotation: how do we rotate keys without invalidating lots of in-flight headers?

lia: plan: signer uses short-lived key epochs (e.g., 1h). header carries resolve_epoch id. Downstream should accept signatures from current and previous epoch for a short grace period. We'll publish epoch-to-key mapping from KMS service with TTL. Also opaque revocation list for compromised keys.

matt: what about clients that re-sign or tamper? We need HMAC with secret only known to proxies, downstream validates; rejects unsigned or bad sigs. Also log invalid-sig rate.

sara: rollout strategy suggestion: internal dev -> select services -> org-wide. Canary metrics to monitor:
- rw.billing.header_accept_rate
- rw.billing.invalid_sig_rate
- rw.billing.fallback_rate
- rw.ingress.proxy_extra_latency_p50/p95
- rw.cost.delta_header_vs_lookup_p95 (histogram of attribution delta)
alert if invalid_sig_rate > 0.1% for 5m or delta > 2% for 10m.

pranav: sampling interplay: if traces are sampled downstream but header arrives at ingress and then gets dropped, we still need a way to reconcile cost for sampled traces. Option to emit a small metadata event to statsd with mapping id that goes to analytics (no PII).

lia: agreed. we'll emit anonymized mapping to a short-lived topic for 24h if header present and the event was sampled. That lets us re-run joins if attribution changes. This event contains only mapping-id, resolve_version, and non-PII tag.

matt: edge case: cross-proxy retry where first proxy attached header A, retry goes to proxy B which resolves B (different token) because of stale cache -> inconsistent header per attempt. downstream might see two different headers for same logical request.

sara: mitigation: include request-id in header-checksum and downstream must prefer earliest header by resolve_version then by sig epoch. Also proxies should honor an incoming X-Request-Id and not overwrite header if present unless incoming header is invalid.

lia: security/regulatory note: tenants can opt out of resolved tokens. In that case proxies send a privacy-flag and downstream will always go to lookup flow. By default, new enterprise tenants get opt-in and can choose HSM-backed signing.

pranav: can we compress header for high-rate flows? e.g., numeric short token id + global mapping table rather than full string per request?

matt: yes, we can use compact token ids (uint32) for internal tenants and reserve long ids for external. mapping TTL in upstream registry keeps it fresh. That saves bytes at cost of registry lookups during key rotation.

sara: test plan:
- unit parser + fuzzing for unknown fields.
- integration: proxy bench with synthetic cache hit/miss ratios.
- canary: route 0.5% traffic for 24h with verbose logging.
- compare attribution via nightly job to baseline.

obs-bot: deploy: cost-hint-canary enabled in eu-central-1 (cohort=0.5%).

lia: open action items:
- lia: write header spec + signer epoch protocol (PR by EOD Friday)
- matt: add cross-proxy retry tests + p95 perf suite
- pranav: spec opt-out/tenant config + privacy review
- sara: canary dashboard + alert rules

pranav: tiny nit: include TTL encoded in header? so downstream can reject stale resolves without consulting registry.

lia: will add ttl field (t=seconds) to header. thanks. I'll post PR link when ready. :sparkles:
